lines.trans: What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down Wutong Lane!

words.gloss: hunt for treasure; go on a treasure hunt

lines.trans: Let us check the brass compass first: east runs straight toward the corner bakery.
Read Clue Card One aloud, Qing, so we do not miss a single word.

words.gloss: measure word for flat surfaces and paper

lines.trans: Card One says: Twenty paces east where cool clear water greets the morning birds.

words.gloss: measure word for flat surfaces and paper

lines.trans: Easy! That is the little carved stone fountain at the end of our block!
Wait, Manager Zhou—whose paces are we counting, yours or mine?
Good question, because Manager Zhou walks like he is chasing a departing bus!
Very funny, Qing; let us walk side by side at a polite normal step.
Five, ten, fifteen... eighteen, nineteen, and twenty paces right to the kerb!
Look ahead—two sparrows are splashing on the rim of the stone fountain!
Thirty years later, the morning birds are still keeping their appointment!
Now look closely at Card One to see what symbol we need to find.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yī. Changes tone to yí before 4th tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd tones (一杯 yì bēi).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yì qǐ. Placed right before the verb to mean 'together' (一起吃晚饭 'have dinner together').

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

examples.text: 等等，让我把平板屏幕和纸本子放一起看。
examples.trans: Wait—let me look at the tablet screen and the paper ledger side by side.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sān shí. Cardinal number thirty ('three tens'); pairs directly with measure words like 三十年 ('thirty years').

examples.text: 这棵老树在院子里长了三十年。
examples.trans: This old tree has grown in the courtyard for thirty years.

examples.text: 从客栈走到地铁站只要三十分钟。
examples.trans: Walking from the inn to the metro station takes only thirty minutes.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dōng. Cardinal direction; 往东走 ('walk east'), 东边 ('the east side').

examples.text: 出了小院大门，顺着梧桐巷往东数二十步就到了。
examples.trans: Step out the courtyard gate and count twenty paces east along Wutong Lane to get there.

examples.text: 清晨的阳光从东边的窗户照进九号房。
examples.trans: Early morning sunlight shines into Room Nine through the eastern window.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎng. Used instead of 二 when counting things with a measure word (两个, 两把, 两间).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gè. Most common Mandarin measure word (量词), placed between a number/demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǔ. Cardinal number 9.

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

examples.text: 九分钟！牛奶、鸡蛋和苹果都买来了！
examples.trans: Nine minutes! The milk, eggs, and apples are all here!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yě. Always stands directly before the verb or adjective, never at the end of a clause.

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 周经理早！桌子很干净，钥匙也准备好了。
examples.trans: Morning, Manager Zhou! The desk is clean, and the keys are ready too.

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Two tens: èrshí.

examples.text: 他二十岁了。
examples.trans: He is twenty years old.

examples.text: 看了二十年电视。
examples.trans: Watched television for twenty years.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǔ. Cardinal number 5.

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

examples.text: 二十五年前我在附近教钢琴，不过记忆淡了。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano nearby, though memories fade.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shén me. Asks 'what?' on its own (什么？) or modifies a noun (什么茶 'what kind of tea').

examples.text: 太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
examples.trans: Great. Please tell me what I need to know.

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǐ xì. Describes checking details or listening closely.

examples.text: 仔细看这一页——记的是分贝和安静度，不是酒店星级！
examples.trans: Look closely at this page—it records decibels and quietness, not hotel stars!

examples.text: 出门前请仔细检查一下门锁。
examples.trans: Please check the door lock carefully before going out.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǐ hòu. Measure word (量词): 段, e.g. 以后的时间 ('time afterward').

examples.text: 三年前爷爷去世以后，我和志鹏因为卖老房子大吵了一架。
examples.trans: Three years ago after Grandfather passed away, Zhipeng and I argued bitterly over selling the old house.

examples.text: 十二点以后再拆吧，老板！看钟：差五分十二点！
examples.trans: Open it after twelve, boss! Look at the clock: five minutes to twelve!

meanings.note: Slightly literary/polished synonym of 仍然.

examples.text: 忙了一整夜，他精神依然很好。
examples.trans: After working all night, his spirits are still high.

examples.text: 多年过去，她依然热爱电视行业。
examples.trans: Years later, she still loves television.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiàng. Introduces a likeness or example ('look like, be like').

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: 他长得真像他哥哥。
examples.trans: He really looks like his older brother.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiān. Placed before the verb to sequence actions: 先…再… ('first…, then…').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bā. Cardinal number 8.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 七点半有八位饿肚子的客人下楼啊！
examples.trans: At seven thirty, eight hungry guests are coming downstairs!

meanings.note: Pinyin: gōngjiāochē. Measure word: 辆.

examples.text: 我每天坐公交车去上班。
examples.trans: I take the bus to work every day.

examples.text: 公交车站就在前面不远。
examples.trans: The bus stop is just a short distance ahead.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiě. Used for writing characters, notes, letters, or reviews.

examples.text: 到星期五？没写名字，也没签名！
examples.trans: Until Friday? No name written, and no signature either!

examples.text: 只剩三十五分钟了！他肯定会写一星差评！
examples.trans: Only thirty-five minutes left! He will surely write a one-star bad review!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǔn shí. Praises trains or guests arriving right on schedule.

examples.text: 我？哦，我只是喜欢准时！七点十四分真美妙！
examples.trans: Me? Oh, I simply love punctuality! Seven fourteen is a lovely minute!

examples.text: 早上七点半的火车一向很准时。
examples.trans: The seven-thirty morning train is always right on time.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chū lái. Directional complement for coming out or figuring something out (认出来).

examples.text: 明信片上整齐的方格字，我两秒钟就认出来了。
examples.trans: That neat block handwriting on the postcard—I recognized it in two seconds.

examples.text: 看合页边露出来的折纸图纸——一楼画着一扇暗门！
examples.trans: Look at the folded blueprint sticking out of the hinge—a hidden door is drawn on the ground floor!

related.gloss: come fresh out of the oven

meanings.note: Pinyin: gāng. Placed right before a verb to show the action happened moments ago.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

examples.text: 一到七号钥匙全拿走了，八号房刚刷了油漆。
examples.trans: Every key from one to seven is taken, and room eight just got fresh paint.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bié. Most commonly means 'do not' in polite commands (别担心 'don't worry'); as a verb, 'pin/clip on'.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 您先坐下，别着急，我们马上看行李牌。
examples.trans: Please sit down first and do not worry; we will check the luggage tag right away.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dào. Works as main verb ('arrive') or result complement ('succeed in reaching/perceiving', 找到, 听到).

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kè. Used as a verb for carving wood/stone (刻着) or noun/classifier for 15 minutes (一刻).

examples.text: 等一下……梧桐巷十二号，角落里还写着两个童年名字的首字母！
examples.trans: Wait a moment... Number twelve, Wutong Lane, with two childhood initials written in the corner!

examples.text: 木头盒上刻着他的名字。
examples.trans: His name is carved onto the wooden box.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qián mian. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 最前面 ('the very front').

examples.text: 前面锁扣有个小锁孔，再看底下贴着：一把旧铜钥匙！
examples.trans: There is a tiny keyhole on the front latch, and taped underneath: an old brass key!

examples.text: 前面路口往右拐就是火车站。
examples.trans: Turn right at the intersection ahead and you are at the station.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shí. Cardinal number 10; building block for 11–99.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Numeral shíwǔ ('fifteen').

examples.text: 方案会还有十五分钟就要开始了。
examples.trans: The proposal meeting starts in fifteen minutes.

examples.text: 中场休息一共是十五分钟。
examples.trans: Intermission lasts fifteen minutes in total.

meanings.note: Small paper card for notes, gifts, or study.

examples.text: 礼物盒里放着一张小卡片。
examples.trans: Inside the gift box sits a small card.

examples.text: 他在卡片上写了几句祝福。
examples.trans: He wrote a few wishes on the card.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qù. Movement away from the speaker, as main verb (去车站) or directional complement (上去).

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǐ. Read zhǐ as the adverb 'only' before verbs, and zhī as a measure word for cups, boxes, and small animals.

examples.text: 而且他今晚八点到这里——只剩四十分钟了！
examples.trans: And he arrives here at eight o'clock this evening—in forty minutes!

examples.text: 只剩三十五分钟了！他肯定会写一星差评！
examples.trans: Only thirty-five minutes left! He will surely write a one-star bad review!

meanings.note: Pinyin: ba. At the end of a sentence, softens commands into friendly suggestions ('let's…') or asks for confirmation.

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ya. Gentle exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 呀，这就是星期一火车上那只双胞胎箱子吗？
examples.trans: Oh, is this that twin suitcase from Monday's train?

meanings.note: Pinyin: ne. After a noun, asks 'what about X?' (你呢？); at the end of a statement, highlights an ongoing situation.

examples.text: 等一下，咖啡厅的小美正朝我招手呢！
examples.trans: Wait a moment—Mei in the café is waving toward me right now!

examples.text: 来成都的第一个晚上，怎么能难过呢！
examples.trans: On your very first evening in Chengdu, how could you sit around sad!

meanings.note: Pinyin: la. Colloquial fusion of 了 + 啊 adding cheerful energy at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 你们守着，我出门啦！
examples.trans: Hold the fort—I am heading out the door!

meanings.note: Pinyin: pēn quán. Measure word (量词): 座 (zuò), e.g. 一座喷泉 ('a fountain').

examples.text: 听得很清楚。你站在小石头喷泉旁边吗？
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you standing beside the little stone fountain?

examples.text: 小广场中间有一座石头喷泉。
examples.trans: There is a stone fountain in the middle of the small plaza.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huí tóu. Appears in the friendly farewell 回头见！ ('See you soon!').

examples.text: 我先去送热茶，我们回头聊！
examples.trans: Let me deliver this hot tea first—we will talk soon!

examples.text: 今天辛苦了，回头见！
examples.trans: Great work today—see you soon!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yīn wèi. Introduces a reason; often paired with 所以 ('therefore') in the next clause.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 因为楼梯窄，而且周经理在那儿放了旧灯箱子。
examples.trans: Because the stairs are narrow, and Manager Zhou put old lamp boxes up there.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. As main verb/preposition, gives location (在院子里); before another verb, marks ongoing action ('be doing').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà shēng. Combines 大 ('big/loud') + 声 ('voice/sound'); modifies verbs of speaking or reading directly (大声念 'read aloud').

examples.text: 小晴，把木牌上的字大声念给我听听吧。
examples.trans: Qing, read the words on the wooden sign aloud for me to hear.

examples.text: 周经理在院子里大声宣布九号房咖啡角正式通过了审核。
examples.trans: In the courtyard, Manager Zhou announced aloud that the Room Nine café corner had officially passed the review.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tiān qì. Measure word (量词): 种 (zhǒng), e.g. 一种好天气 ('pleasant weather').

examples.text: 我在看天气，小美！铃铛旁边这封厚信是谁放的？
examples.trans: I am checking the weather, Mei! Who put this thick letter beside the bell?

examples.text: 今天天气晴朗，最适合晒被子。
examples.trans: Today's weather is bright and sunny—ideal for airing quilts.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tài. Often frames 太 + adj + 了 for warm exclamations (太好了！ 'Wonderful!').

examples.text: 太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
examples.trans: Great. Please tell me what I need to know.

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎo. Main adjective 'good'; as a result complement after a verb, means 'ready/completed properly' (修好, 准备好).

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎoxiào.

examples.text: 他讲的笑话一点都不好笑。
examples.trans: The joke he told was not funny at all.

examples.text: 我觉得这个故事非常好笑。
examples.trans: I find this story very hilarious.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zì. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个字 ('a written character').

examples.text: 真好奇！那张行李牌上的字看着很眼熟。
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on that tag looked very familiar.

examples.text: 先别对外面透露一个字！让两兄弟先过完这个星期五下午！
examples.trans: Not a single word to anyone outside yet! Let the two brothers have their Friday afternoon first!

寻宝.gloss: hunt for treasure; go on a treasure hunt

meanings.en: hunt for treasure; go on a treasure hunt
meanings.note: Pinyin: xún bǎo. Verb-object compound (寻 'seek' + 宝 'treasure'); 寻宝队 = 'treasure-hunting crew'.

examples.text: 早上好，寻宝队！我给大家端了三杯热咖啡过来。
examples.trans: Good morning, treasure hunters! I brought three hot mugs of coffee out for everyone.

examples.text: 星期六上午，大家拿着指南针去梧桐巷寻宝。
examples.trans: On Saturday morning, everyone heads down Wutong Lane with the compass on a treasure hunt.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎo. Everyday adjective for small size; also prefixes younger colleagues' names warmly (小晴, 小美).

examples.text: 早上好，姑娘。我有一个宋名下的预订。
examples.trans: Good morning, young lady. I have a booking for Song.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiáo niǎo. Measure word (量词): 只 (zhǐ), e.g. 一只小鸟 ('a little bird').

examples.text: 没错。外面大街很吵，进了院子却只听见树叶和小鸟。
examples.trans: Exactly. Outside on the main road it is noisy, yet inside the courtyard you only hear leaves and birds.

examples.text: 早上树上有两只小鸟在唱歌。
examples.trans: Two little birds are singing in the tree this morning.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù shì. Adds emphatic certainty before a noun ('is the very one').

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

examples.text: 没关系！您就是志豪先生吧？
examples.trans: No problem at all! You must be Mr Zhihao, right?

meanings.note: Pinyin: nián. Time classifier taking no 个 directly after numbers (六年 'six years', 今年 'this year').

examples.text: 二十五年前我在附近教钢琴，不过记忆淡了。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano nearby, though memories fade.

examples.text: 老橡木，八十年了，一滴水都不漏。
examples.trans: Old oak, eighty years old—not a single drop leaks.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bìngpái.

examples.text: 他们两人并排走在小路上。
examples.trans: The two of them walked side by side on the path.

examples.text: 这两栋楼是并排建的。
examples.trans: These two buildings were built side by side.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kāi. Versatile verb for opening doors, starting business, turning on taps/lights, or water boiling.

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 当然不能偷看……咦，自己翻开在中间那页了！
examples.trans: Of course we must not peek... oh, it fell open to the middle page by itself!

张.gloss: measure word for flat surfaces and paper

meanings.en: measure word for flat surfaces and paper
meanings.note: Pinyin: zhāng. Counts tables, beds, paper sheets, tickets, receipts, and luggage tags (一张桌子, 一张纸).

examples.text: 不在，只有我的笔和三张旧收据！
examples.trans: Not there—only my pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: 旁边的把手上系着一张小纸牌。
examples.trans: There is a small paper card tied on the side handle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎng. Guides movement in directions (往上提 'lift upward', 往左拐 'turn left').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Read de after a verb to introduce how it goes (走得快 'walk fast'); read děi before a verb to mean 'must'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: niàn. Used for reading a letter or notice out loud (念第一行 'read the first line aloud').

examples.text: 二十毫米、铜的、热水器阀门——我一路念过去！
examples.trans: Twenty millimetres, brass, water-heater valve—I will repeat it all the way!

examples.text: 十九条理由？！您是迎接哥哥，还是念火车时刻表呀？
examples.trans: Nineteen reasons?! Are you welcoming your brother or reading a train timetable?

meanings.note: Pinyin: nín. Respectful singular 'you' used with elders, teachers, and guests (您好！).

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ. First-person singular pronoun; add 的 for 'my' (我的) and 们 for 'we/us' (我们).

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ men. First-person plural pronoun; add 的 for 'our' (我们的).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǎo. Focuses on searching; add 到 (找到) for actually finding.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: 我正在打……您好，请问有人找蓝色行李箱吗？
examples.trans: I am calling now... Hello, excuse me, is anyone looking for a blue suitcase?

meanings.en: measure word for handled objects; disposal marker
meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎ. Counts items with handles or backs (一把钥匙, 一把椅子); as a preposition, fronts a definite object before an action verb.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǐ nán zhēn. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个指南针 ('a compass'). Literally 'south-pointing needle'.

examples.text: 小晴手里拿着黄铜指南针，顺着梧桐巷往东走。
examples.trans: Holding the brass compass in hand, Qing walks east along Wutong Lane.

examples.text: 这个实心黄铜指南针埋在地下三十年，依然非常准。
examples.trans: Buried underground for thirty years, this solid brass compass is still remarkably accurate.

meanings.note: Noun shù ('count; certainty in 心里有数').

examples.text: 你以为雷总心里一点数都没有吗？
examples.trans: Do you think Director Lei has no idea what goes on?

examples.text: 经费还剩多少，我心里有数。
examples.trans: I have a clear count of how much budget remains.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǎo shang. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个早上 ('a morning').

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī liù. Literally 'week-day six'; Mainland standard alongside informal 周六 (zhōu liù).

examples.text: 每个星期六早上，这条老街都有热闹的集市。
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning, this old street hosts a lively market.

examples.text: 星期六下午来院子里喝杯热柠檬茶吧。
examples.trans: Come to the courtyard for a cup of hot lemon tea on Saturday afternoon.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cháo. Describes which way a window faces or waving toward someone (朝院子 'facing the courtyard').

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

examples.text: 朝院子，就在老树上面，非常安静。
examples.trans: Toward the courtyard, right above the old tree; it is very quiet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lái. Movement toward the speaker, as main verb or directional complement (进来 'come in').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 大门口正好来了一辆出租车。
examples.trans: A taxi has just pulled up right at the front gate.

meanings.en: right in the middle of; squarely; right
meanings.note: Pinyin: zhèng. Before a verb, marks an action in progress right now; before 对着, means 'directly/squarely'.

examples.text: 正合我心意。楼梯在哪儿？
examples.trans: Just what I wanted. Where are the stairs?

examples.text: 等一下，咖啡厅的小美正朝我招手呢！
examples.trans: Wait a moment—Mei in the café is waving toward me right now!

meanings.en: just right; happen to; right on the dot
meanings.note: Pinyin: zhèng hǎo. Marks a lucky coincidence or exact fit.

examples.text: 大门口正好来了一辆出租车。
examples.trans: A taxi has just pulled up right at the front gate.

examples.text: 他拿旧阀门比对了——架子上正好还剩两个！
examples.trans: He matched it against the old valve—he has two left on the shelf!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhèng cháng. Describes normal water pressure or normal operation.

examples.text: 电线本来就该拉直了。正常保养，别多想。
examples.trans: The wire needed straightening anyway. Routine maintenance—don't read into it.

examples.text: 修好阀门以后，三楼水压完全正常了。
examples.trans: After fixing the valve, third-floor water pressure is completely normal.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bù. Counts footsteps or stages (一步 'one step').

examples.text: 真的？您不介意多爬几步楼梯？
examples.trans: Really? You do not mind climbing a few extra stairs?

examples.text: 茶壶也烫好了！大家从窗边退后一步！
examples.trans: And the teapot is hot! Everybody step back from the window!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bùzi. Measure word: 步.

examples.text: 他的步子迈得很大。
examples.trans: He takes very large steps.

examples.text: 她放慢了步子，等后面的人跟上。
examples.trans: She slowed her pace to wait for the people behind to catch up.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuǐ. Measure word (量词): 杯 (bēi), e.g. 一杯水 ('a glass of water').

examples.text: 老橡木，八十年了，一滴水都不漏。
examples.trans: Old oak, eighty years old—not a single drop leaks.

examples.text: 摸摸热水管——下面是温的，上面变凉了。
examples.trans: Feel the hot-water pipe—the bottom is warm, while the top is turning cool.

related.gloss: a glass of water (measure word 杯)

meanings.note: Pinyin: qīngliáng.

examples.text: 夏天的夜晚有一阵清凉的风。
examples.trans: There is a cool breeze on the summer night.

examples.text: 喝一杯冰水感觉非常清凉。
examples.trans: Drinking a glass of ice water feels very refreshing.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lòu. Used for leaking pipes or roofs (漏水) and omitted items.

examples.text: 老橡木，八十年了，一滴水都不漏。
examples.trans: Old oak, eighty years old—not a single drop leaks.

examples.text: 一滴水都不漏！现在可以点着热水器了吗？
examples.trans: Not a single drop leaking! Can we light the water heater now?

meanings.note: Verb wán ('play; pull a stunt').

examples.text: 你自己也知道昨晚玩得太过火了吧？
examples.trans: Even you know last night's stunt went too far, right?

examples.text: 周末休息的时候大家一起出去玩。
examples.trans: Everyone goes out to relax over the weekend.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiàn zài. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 现在这时候 ('this moment right now').

examples.text: 现在他的箱子还安全锁着呢。
examples.trans: For now, his suitcase stays safely locked up.

examples.text: 太好了！现在我想吃一顿丰盛的早餐。
examples.trans: Wonderful! Now I would like to eat a big breakfast.

related.gloss: this moment right now (measure word 个)

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòng. Works as main verb ('use a key') or preposition ('with/using').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 别担心！用冰气泡水一擦，橙汁就掉。
examples.trans: Do not worry! Wipe it once with cold sparkling water and orange juice comes right out.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: kàn. Covers looking at something, reading silently, or visiting someone; add 见/到 for 'catch sight of'.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: 老板，看一下桌子后面的镜子。
examples.trans: Boss, take a look in the mirror behind the desk.

meanings.en: take a look; have a quick look
meanings.note: Pinyin: kàn kan. Friendly reduplicated form of 看.

examples.text: 快拿到楼下灯光下面看看吧！
examples.trans: Let's bring it downstairs under the light and take a look!

examples.text: 哎呀，怎么拿错了！我戴眼镜看看行李牌。
examples.trans: Dear me, what a mix-up! Let me put on my glasses and check the luggage tag.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhēn. Exclamatory adverb before adjectives (真好！ 'How nice!') or adjective 'genuine'.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

examples.text: 真奇怪！我们坐同一班早火车到同一个区。
examples.trans: How strange! We rode the very same morning train to the same district.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhe. Placed right after a verb to show a state or posture continues (门开着 'the door stands open').

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shí tou. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块石头 ('a stone').

examples.text: 我来帮您。哎呀，里面装了石头吗？
examples.trans: Let me help you. Goodness, did you pack stones inside?

examples.text: 等等，低头看石头台阶上。
examples.trans: Wait—look down on the stone step.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǐ mào. Measure word (量词): 种 (zhǒng), e.g. 一种礼貌 ('good manners').

examples.text: 声音轻，很有礼貌，大概三十多岁，有点紧张。
examples.trans: Soft-spoken, very polite, around thirty-something, and a bit nervous.

examples.text: 小伙子对每位长辈说话都很有礼貌。
examples.trans: The young man speaks politely to every elder.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dì. Placed before any number to turn it into an ordinal (第一 'first', 第二天 'the second day').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: děng deng. Urgent or casual reduplication of 等 ('wait!').

examples.text: 等等，深蓝色的，跟您的一样啊！
examples.trans: Wait—it is dark blue, the same as yours!

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎn dān. Everyday adjective for straightforward tasks.

examples.text: 挺起肩膀，志豪先生。记住那三句简单的话——我去开门！
examples.trans: Shoulders back, Mr Zhihao. Remember those three simple lines—I will open the gate!

examples.text: 这道炒蛋做法很简单，味道却极好。
examples.trans: This scrambled-egg recipe is simple, yet tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Noun xiànsuǒ ('investigative lead').

examples.text: 是你们自己走漏了风声，才让我有了线索。
examples.trans: Your own leak was what gave me the lead.

examples.text: 记者顺着这条小线索查清了来龙去脉。
examples.trans: Following that small lead, the reporter pieced it together.

meanings.note: Verb/noun huā ('spend time/money').

examples.text: 我花了六年的时间学习电视节目制作。
examples.trans: I spent six full years studying TV production.

examples.text: 这笔宣传预算必须花在刀刃上。
examples.trans: This publicity budget must be spent where it counts.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiē kǒu. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个街口 ('a street corner').

examples.text: 听……街口钟楼开始敲十二下了！
examples.trans: Listen... the clock tower at the end of the street is starting to strike twelve!

examples.text: 出了院门走到街口就能打到出租车。
examples.trans: Walk out the gate to the end of the lane and you can hail a cab.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiē jiǎo. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个街角 ('a street corner').

examples.text: 先别灰心坐下！继续往街角看。
examples.trans: Do not sit down discouraged yet! Keep looking toward the street corner.

examples.text: 街角那家绿色招牌的药店九点开门。
examples.trans: That green-signed pharmacy on the corner opens at nine.

meanings.en: want; need; will / be going to
meanings.note: Pinyin: yào. Direct verb for ordering/requesting ('want'), obligation ('need to'), or imminent future (要下雨了).

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiàn. Appears in farewells (再见, 明天见) and as result complement of perception (看见, 听见).

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

examples.text: 老陈，听得见吗？我刚经过绿药店！
examples.trans: Chen, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jì hao. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè). Joins 记 ('to record') + 号 ('symbol'). Neutral tone on the second syllable.

examples.text: 树干上刻着一个三角形的记号。
examples.trans: A triangular mark is carved into the tree trunk.

examples.text: 老陈在修好的管子上画了个红色的记号。
examples.trans: Chen drew a red mark on the repaired pipe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuí. Question pronoun for people; stays in the exact spot of the answer (这是谁的？ 'Whose is this?').

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 一点没破！是谁送回来的？
examples.trans: Not cracked at all! Who brought it back?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǒu. Means 'walk' (走路, 直走) or 'leave / head off' (我先走了).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǒu lù. Separable verb-object compound 走 ('walk') + 路 ('road'); placed before 去 + place to mean 'walk to…'.

examples.text: 星期六集市离客栈很近，我们走路去只要五分钟。
examples.trans: The Saturday market is right near the inn—it only takes us five minutes to walk there.

examples.text: 吃过晚饭去河边走走路，浑身都舒服。
examples.trans: Taking a walk by the river after dinner makes you feel great all over.

meanings.note: Formal verb-object fùyuē ('attend a scheduled meeting').

examples.text: 淳于先生肯来赴约，很给面子呀。
examples.trans: Mr Chun Yuqiao keeping our appointment does me great honour.

examples.text: 尽管工作很忙，他还是准时赶来赴约了。
examples.trans: Despite a packed schedule, he arrived on time for the meeting.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lù biān. Measure word (量词): 排 (pái), e.g. 路边小树 ('roadside trees').

examples.text: 别动，你们俩。听到路边汽车停下的声音了吗？
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. Hear that car engine stopping at the curb?

examples.text: 路边新开了一家卖热豆浆的小早点铺。
examples.trans: A breakfast stall selling hot soy milk just opened by the roadside.

meanings.note: Pinyin: biān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一边 ('one side').

examples.text: 对，过了桥，右手边会经过一家绿药店。
examples.trans: Right, after crossing the bridge, you pass a green pharmacy on your right.

examples.text: 快坐在向阳窗户边，宋老师！先别急着上楼！
examples.trans: Sit right down by the sunny window, Teacher Song! No rush to go back upstairs yet!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yíng jiē. Used for stepping out to greet an arriving guest.

examples.text: 十九条理由？！您是迎接哥哥，还是念火车时刻表呀？
examples.trans: Nineteen reasons?! Are you welcoming your brother or reading a train timetable?

examples.text: 有进步！今天小院迎接兄弟重逢——大家保持安静端庄！
examples.trans: Progress! Today our courtyard hosts a brotherly reunion—quiet dignity from everyone!

meanings.note: Pinyin: hái shi. Joins choices in questions (茶还是咖啡？ 'tea or coffee?') or means 'still'.

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

examples.text: 宋老师早！您想喝咖啡还是红茶？
examples.trans: Morning, Teacher Song! Would you like coffee or black tea?

examples.text: 你这半辈子都没追过人，都是人追你的。
examples.trans: Half your life you have never chased anyone — people have always chased you.

examples.text: 这件事我们再商量一下。
examples.trans: Let's discuss this matter a bit more.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sù dù. Measure word (量词): 种 (zhǒng), e.g. 一种速度 ('a speed').

examples.text: 速度真快！店主给你收据了吗？
examples.trans: Impressive speed! Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?

examples.text: 两个人一起摆桌子，速度比平时快一倍。
examples.trans: With two people setting tables together, it goes twice as fast.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà. Distal demonstrative before measure words (那个 'that one'); at clause start, means 'then / well then'.

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà tóu. Colloquial locative noun ('the far end / across'), contrasting with 这头 ('this end').

examples.text: 哪怕坐在阳光房那头，也能听清钢琴的旋律。
examples.trans: Even sitting at the far end of the sunroom, you can hear the piano melody clearly.

examples.text: 老陈在走廊那头喊我们过去帮忙扶书架。
examples.trans: From the other end of the corridor, Chen called us over to help steady the bookcase.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wèn. Everyday verb for asking a question (请问 'may I ask').

examples.text: 等等——先生您好！您问那个深蓝色行李箱吗？
examples.trans: Wait—hello, sir! Are you asking about that dark-blue suitcase?

examples.text: 快问他叫什么名字！记下来！
examples.trans: Quick, ask him what his name is! Write it down!

meanings.note: Pinyin: miànbāodiàn. Measure word: 家.

examples.text: 这家面包店的牛角包很好吃。
examples.trans: The croissants at this bakery are very delicious.

examples.text: 早上空气里飘着面包店的香味。
examples.trans: The smell of the bakery wafted through the morning air.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shùn zhe. Preposition 顺 ('follow along in the same direction') + continuous particle 着 (顺着走廊吹 'blow down the hallway', 顺着木纹刷 'brush along the wood grain').

examples.text: 小晴顺着木纹薄薄地刷油漆，刷出来的窗板又平整又漂亮。
examples.trans: Qing brushed the paint thinly along the wood grain, giving the shutters a smooth, even finish.

examples.text: 顺着梧桐巷的青石板路一直往前走，就能看见九号房的木牌。
examples.trans: Walk straight along the flagstones of Wutong Lane and you will spot the wooden sign for Room Nine.

meanings.note: Pinyin: máquè. Measure word: 只.

examples.text: 几只麻雀在地上啄食。
examples.trans: Several sparrows were pecking at food on the ground.

examples.text: 虽然麻雀很小，但飞得很快。
examples.trans: Although the sparrow is small, it flies very fast.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huáng tóng. Literally 黄 ('yellow/golden') + 铜 ('copper/bronze'): copper-zinc brass alloy.

examples.text: 钢琴琴槌里面的细小轴销是用结实的黄铜做的。
examples.trans: The tiny hinge pins inside piano hammers are made of sturdy brass.

examples.text: 老陈把前台的黄铜小铃铛擦得金光发亮。
examples.trans: Chen polished the little brass bell on the front desk until it gleamed.
